- **[Disruption with some GitHub services](../../../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-ecff77931aa1.md)** - github; `unknown` / `high`. Nov 19, 18:17 UTC Resolved - Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time. We mitigated the incident by deploying a fix to ensure that continued web activity renews session expiration and browser cookies. We are adding monitoring to detect unexpected drops in session renewal activity, helping us catch similar issues sooner and reduce their impact on users. Nov 19, 18:05 UTC Update - The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability. Nov 19, 17:43 UTC Monitoring - Starting around 18:02 UTC on November 5, GitHub web sessions stopped being renewed based on recent activity, so users were signed out when their sessions expired due to inactivity. - **[Disruption with some GitHub services](../../../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-ecff77931aa1.md)** - github; `unknown` / `high`. Nov 19, 18:17 UTC Resolved - Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time. We mitigated the incident by deploying a fix to ensure that continued web activity renews session expiration and browser cookies. We are adding monitoring to detect unexpected drops in session renewal activity, helping us catch similar issues sooner and reduce their impact on users. Nov 19, 18:05 UTC Update - The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability. Nov 19, 17:43 UTC Monitoring - Starting around 18:02 UTC on November 5, GitHub web sessions stopped being renewed based on recent activity, so users were signed out when their sessions expired due to inactivity. These sign-outs were caused by a bug in session renewal, not due to a security incident. We believe we fixed... [Source](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/m310qbkfm3ww)

- **[Increased timeouts due to surge in anonymous users](../../../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-62865e66e8b1.md)** - github; `unknown` / `low`. Nov 9, 09:09 UTC Resolved - On November 9, 2026, GitHub.com experienced intermittent timeouts between approximately 05:10 and 08:15 UTC. Across that full window, 6.5% of recorded requests to github.com timed out, with a five-minute peak of 13.9% between 07:40 and 07:45 UTC. Release downloads were more affected: 38.5% of recorded requests timed out, peaking at 76% during that same five-minute interval. The two main error waves lasted about two hours and ten minutes in total, with recovery between them. The errors affected repository browsing and disrupted some CI workflows and Copilot code review jobs. Contrary to our earlier updates, follow-up analysis confirmed at least 6,236 authenticated requests that timed out, affecting activity feeds, access to uploaded attachments and repository archive downloads. Errors occurred during elevated traffic to our web infrastructure that handles unauthenticated requests. Impact was mitigated when traffic causing pressure on this system was alleviated. Our follow-up work focuses on improving capacity monitoring, traffic prioritization improvements, and automated protection against traffic spikes. Nov 9, 09:09 UTC Update - We are resolving this... - **[Increased task-related errors for Copilot Mission Control](../../../../../knowledge/GitHub/updates/2026/github-status-history-github-5ddabf82590b.md)** - github; `unknown` / `low`. Nov 4, 10:01 UTC Resolved - On November 4, 2026, between approximately 03:40 UTC and 10:01 UTC, some Copilot agent users experienced errors listing and creating agent tasks. On average, 1.22% of requests were failed, with a peak of 2.68% over a ten-minute interval. The issue occurred when increased task-list traffic and expensive queries exhausted shared database capacity. We mitigated the broader impact by disabling a client experiment and temporarily restricting task-list requests from the affected client. Task-list requests remained restricted after the wider service recovered; we removed the blanket restriction on November 6 and continued a gradual rollout. We’ve since improved task-list queries, moved rate limiting to separate infrastructure and added capacity monitoring. We’re continuing to reduce unnecessary client requests and validate capacity before expanding the rollout to reduce the chance of recurrence. Nov 4, 10:01 UTC Monitoring - The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability. Nov 4, 09:50 UTC Update - We're continuing to see recovery as rollout continues Nov 4, 09:11 UTC Update - We've identified the issue with a specific client versio...
